items.title: fix(profiles): platform adapters never recreate a deleted profile home
items.author: kshitijk4poor
items.summary: A merged fix stops eight writer code paths in gateway platform plugins from recreating a deleted or renamed profile home via raw mkdir(parents=True) calls. All affected writers now go through mkdir_under_hermes_home, with per-adapter handling retained: Google Chat in-memory counts are skipped, Feishu comment pairing raises rather than falsely reporting a save, and Matrix crypto/recovery-key writes are refused through existing warning and abort paths. This resolves tracker #155595 U3, part 2 of issue #9.
items.reasoning: A systemic fix across multiple platform adapters (Google Chat, Feishu, Matrix and others) addressing a tracked profile-integrity bug; relevant to any user running named profiles with gateway platforms, though it is a bug fix rather than a new capability.

items.content_html:
fix(profiles): platform adapters never recreate a deleted profile home

Eight writers in gateway platform plugins still created their directory with a

raw mkdir(parents=True) under the active profile home. An adapter bound to a

named profile that was deleted or renamed meanwhile brought profiles/<name>/

back on its next write (tracker #155595 U3, part 2 of #9).

They now go through mkdir_under_hermes_home; each keeps its existing handling:

  • Google Chat thread-count store: skipped, counts stay in memory;
  • Feishu comment pairing: raises, so an approval is never reported saved;
  • Matrix crypto store (connect and E2EE setup) and recovery-key target and

write: refused through the existing reason / warning / abort paths;

line-neutral (the adapter is over the 2000-line cap);

  • the auth.json lock helper (_file_lock): raises before a lock file is created;

Photon's stores take it before writing, so the lock recreated a renamed home

first. Line-neutral (auth.py is over the cap);

  • Photon auth.json: raises to the auth caller;
  • Photon sidecar mirror: falls back to the source dir like a read-only one;
  • WhatsApp secondary bridge-port record: raises into connect's existing

OSError handling;

  • WhatsApp Cloud inbound media cache: the media is dropped like a failed

write.

Each gets a delete+rename regression that fails on main and on a raw-mkdir

mutant.

items.title: Hermes Agent Discord vs Telegram: Which One Should You Use? (2026)
items.content:
Hermes Agent Discord vs Telegram is the first choice you make once your agent works on your laptop: where do you talk to it from now on? Short version: Telegram is the fastest personal line, Discord is the better home for a team, and one Hermes gateway can run both at the same time. Watch the video below, then read the full breakdown: a side-by-side table from the official docs, who should pick which, the setup for each, and how to run the two together.

Key takeaways

Telegram = one person, phone first: QR setup, voice memos, webhook mode for sleeping cloud hosts.
Discord = teams: a thread per @mention, a session per user, role access, live voice channels.
Both share one gateway, so skills, memory and cron jobs carry over.
File caps differ: 20 MB on Telegram’s public Bot API vs 32 MiB per Discord attachment.

Hermes Agent Discord vs Telegram: the side-by-side table
Both platforms sit in the platform table of the Hermes Messaging Gateway docs. Telegram ticks voice, images, files, threads, typing and streaming. Discord ticks all of those plus reactions. The real differences show up once you read each platform’s own page.

Both use the full Hermes toolset, terminal included: hermes-telegram and hermes-discord.
One gateway, two front doors
Hermes does not run a separate program per app. The hermes gateway process loads each adapter, sends every chat into its own session, and passes it to the agent. It also hosts the cron scheduler, ticking once a minute (every 60 seconds) to fire due jobs.
That is why this choice is low stakes. Your skills, memory and scheduled jobs live in the install. Moving to the other app is a new token, an allowlist line and a restart.

hermes gateway install sets it up as a background service, so it starts on its own.
hermes gateway status tells you if it is running.

Who should pick Telegram
Telegram suits the solo owner. You message the agent from your phone, send a voice memo on the go, and get your scheduled reports in the same chat.

Fastest start. In the dashboard or desktop app: Messaging → Telegram → Create with QR. Hermes makes the bot, detects your user ID and restarts the gateway.
Voice memos. They are transcribed automatically, so talking replaces typing.
Topics for projects. Private Chat Topics (Bot API 9.4, February 2026) give each topic in your DM its own session.
No lost messages. While the gateway is off, Telegram holds new messages for up to 24 hours and Hermes answers them in order on boot.
Cheap cloud hosting. Webhook mode lets hosts like Fly.io, Railway or Render sleep between messages.

Full build: my Hermes Agent Telegram setup guide. For topics, see Hermes Agent Telegram threads.
Who should pick Discord
Discord suits a business where several people hand the agent work.

Thread per job. DISCORD_AUTO_THREAD is on by default: tag the bot in a text channel and the conversation moves into a brand-new thread.
Private sessions in shared rooms. group_sessions_per_user defaults to true, so two staff in one channel never share a transcript.
Role access. DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES lets everyone with a role in. New hires get access the moment they get the role.
Visible progress. Reactions are on: 👀 when a job starts, ✅ on success, ❌ on an error.
Voice rooms. /voice join puts the bot in your voice channel, where it listens, answers out loud and posts the transcript in text.

Full build: my Hermes Agent Discord setup guide.
Groups: privacy mode vs @mention
Most “my bot is broken” messages come from group behaviour, not bugs.
Telegram
Privacy mode is on by default. The bot only sees messages that start with /, replies to its own messages and service messages. To let it read the group, message @BotFather, send /mybots, pick the bot, then Bot Settings → Group Privacy → Turn off. Then remove the bot from the group and add it back, because Telegram stores the setting when the bot joins. Promoting the bot to admin works too. Add telegram.require_mention: true if you only want replies when it is tagged.
Discord
The bot reads channels but only replies when @mentioned (DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION=true). List a help channel in DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS to drop the tag, or silence channels with DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS. The bot is also blocked from pinging @everyone and @here unless you switch that on.

Want a Hermes setup that gives you hours back each week? Join the AI Profit Boardroom → for the step-by-step trainings and four live coaching calls a week.

Join the AI Profit Boardroom →

Voice and files compared
The voice mode docs cover gateway voice for Telegram and Discord together. On both, voice messages are transcribed, and /voice tts adds spoken replies. For transcription you can use Groq Whisper, OpenAI Whisper, or faster-whisper running locally without any key.
Only Discord does live voice. In a voice channel, the bot waits for 1.5 seconds of silence after you speak, pauses its listener while it talks so it never hears itself, and leaves after 300 idle seconds by default.
Files are the other gap. Telegram’s public Bot API stops downloads at 20 MB, and Hermes replies that the file is too large. A local telegram-bot-api server raises that to 2 GB. Discord’s default is 32 MiB per attachment, set by DISCORD_MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES.
Access and safety on both
The gateway denies every user who is not on an allowlist or paired. That is the safe default for a bot that can use a terminal.

Telegram: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS with numeric user IDs (ask @userinfobot for yours).
Discord: DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS (usernames resolve on connect) or DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES.
DM pairing: newcomers get a one-time code, you run hermes pairing approve, and codes expire after an hour.

Everyone you authorise gets full agent access, tools and system included. Keep both lists short.
How to set up Telegram

Fast route: Messaging → Telegram → Create with QR, then scan with your phone.
Manual route: open @BotFather and send /newbot.
Choose any display name, then a unique username that must end in bot, and save the token BotFather replies with.
Run hermes gateway setup, choose Telegram, paste the token and your user ID.
Run hermes gateway and message your bot.

Prefer to edit the file yourself? Add TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS to ~/.hermes/.env. Every step is on the official Telegram setup page.
How to set up Discord

Open the Discord Developer Portal, create an application, then a bot.
Under Privileged Gateway Intents, turn on Server Members Intent and Message Content Intent. Save.
Click Reset Token and copy it. Discord shows it once.
Build the invite URL on the Installation tab, then invite the bot into your server.
Back on your machine, start hermes gateway setup, select Discord and hand it the token.

From there the wizard verifies the token with Discord, flags a disabled Message Content Intent, gives you the invite link and can put you on the allowlist. The official Discord setup page calls that intent the number one reason Discord bots fail: without it, Discord refuses the connection.
Running both on one Hermes gateway
Put both tokens and both allowlists in the same .env, then restart the gateway once. Each app keeps its own chats, while the agent behind them stays the same.
Type /sethome in the chat where scheduled reports should land. Telegram and Discord each have their own home channel, so personal reports can go to Telegram and team updates to a Discord channel.
Running on Hermes Cloud with Team Gateway switched on? Then a shared Hermes bot carries Telegram and Discord traffic for you. Setting GATEWAY_RELAY_ALLOW_DIRECT_PLATFORMS=true allows your own bot as well, at the cost of the instance never sleeping.
Reddit threads in r/hermesagent are split on which app is best, and the docs explain why: both are full platforms. Code and releases are on the Hermes Agent GitHub repo.
Bottom line: solo and mobile, start on Telegram; team and threads, start on Discord; owner plus staff, run both. That is the whole call on Hermes Agent Discord vs Telegram.

FAQ: hermes agent discord vs telegram
Is Discord or Telegram better for Hermes Agent?
Telegram is better for one person who wants a quick phone line to the agent. Discord is better for teams that need threads, roles and voice channels. Both carry the full Hermes toolset.
Can Hermes Agent use Telegram and Discord at the same time?
Yes. One hermes gateway process runs both adapters, and skills, memory and cron jobs are shared between them.
Why does my Telegram bot ignore messages in a group?
Privacy mode is on by default. Turn it off in BotFather under Group Privacy and re-add the bot, or make the bot a group admin.
Why is my Hermes Discord bot offline?
Message Content Intent is almost always off. Turn it on under Privileged Gateway Intents in the Discord Developer Portal and save.
Which app handles bigger files?
Discord, by default: 32 MiB per attachment. Telegram’s public Bot API stops at 20 MB unless you run a local telegram-bot-api server, which allows 2 GB.

Who should pick Telegram

Telegram suits the solo owner. You message the agent from your phone, send a voice memo on the go, and get your scheduled reports in the same chat.

Fastest start. In the dashboard or desktop app: Messaging → Telegram → Create with QR. Hermes makes the bot, detects your user ID and restarts the gateway.

Who should pick Discord

Discord suits a business where several people hand the agent work.

Thread per job. DISCORD_AUTO_THREAD is on by default: tag the bot in a text channel and the conversation moves into a brand-new thread.

Private sessions in shared rooms. group_sessions_per_user defaults to true, so two staff in one channel never share a transcript.

Role access. DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES lets everyone with a role in. New hires get access the moment they get the role.

Visible progress. Reactions are on: 👀 when a job starts, ✅ on success, ❌ on an error.

Voice rooms. /voice join puts the bot in your voice channel, where it listens, answers out loud and posts the transcript in text.

Groups: privacy mode vs @mention

Most “my bot is broken” messages come from group behaviour, not bugs.

Telegram

Privacy mode is on by default. The bot only sees messages that start with /, replies to its own messages and service messages. To let it read the group, message @BotFather, send /mybots, pick the bot, then Bot Settings → Group Privacy → Turn off. Then remove the bot from the group and add it back, because Telegram stores the setting when the bot joins. Promoting the bot to admin works too. Add telegram.require_mention: true if you only want replies when it is tagged.

Discord

The bot reads channels but only replies when @mentioned (DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION=true). List a help channel in DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS to drop the tag, or silence channels with DISCORD_IGNORED_CHANNELS. The bot is also blocked from pinging @everyone and @here unless you switch that on.

Voice and files compared

The voice mode docs cover gateway voice for Telegram and Discord together. On both, voice messages are transcribed, and /voice tts adds spoken replies. For transcription you can use Groq Whisper, OpenAI Whisper, or faster-whisper running locally without any key.

Only Discord does live voice. In a voice channel, the bot waits for 1.5 seconds of silence after you speak, pauses its listener while it talks so it never hears itself, and leaves after 300 idle seconds by default.

Files are the other gap. Telegram’s public Bot API stops downloads at 20 MB, and Hermes replies that the file is too large. A local telegram-bot-api server raises that to 2 GB. Discord’s default is 32 MiB per attachment, set by DISCORD_MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES.

Access and safety on both

The gateway denies every user who is not on an allowlist or paired. That is the safe default for a bot that can use a terminal.

Telegram: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS with numeric user IDs (ask @userinfobot for yours).

Discord: DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS (usernames resolve on connect) or DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES.

DM pairing: newcomers get a one-time code, you run hermes pairing approve, and codes expire after an hour.

Everyone you authorise gets full agent access, tools and system included. Keep both lists short.

How to set up Telegram

Fast route: Messaging → Telegram → Create with QR, then scan with your phone.

Manual route: open @BotFather and send /newbot.

Choose any display name, then a unique username that must end in bot, and save the token BotFather replies with.

Run hermes gateway setup, choose Telegram, paste the token and your user ID.

Run hermes gateway and message your bot.

Prefer to edit the file yourself? Add TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS to ~/.hermes/.env. Every step is on the official Telegram setup page.

How to set up Discord

Open the Discord Developer Portal, create an application, then a bot.

Under Privileged Gateway Intents, turn on Server Members Intent and Message Content Intent. Save.

Click Reset Token and copy it. Discord shows it once.

Build the invite URL on the Installation tab, then invite the bot into your server.

Back on your machine, start hermes gateway setup, select Discord and hand it the token.

From there the wizard verifies the token with Discord, flags a disabled Message Content Intent, gives you the invite link and can put you on the allowlist. The official Discord setup page calls that intent the number one reason Discord bots fail: without it, Discord refuses the connection.

Running both on one Hermes gateway

Put both tokens and both allowlists in the same .env, then restart the gateway once. Each app keeps its own chats, while the agent behind them stays the same.

Type /sethome in the chat where scheduled reports should land. Telegram and Discord each have their own home channel, so personal reports can go to Telegram and team updates to a Discord channel.

Running on Hermes Cloud with Team Gateway switched on? Then a shared Hermes bot carries Telegram and Discord traffic for you. Setting GATEWAY_RELAY_ALLOW_DIRECT_PLATFORMS=true allows your own bot as well, at the cost of the instance never sleeping.

Reddit threads in r/hermesagent are split on which app is best, and the docs explain why: both are full platforms. Code and releases are on the Hermes Agent GitHub repo.

Bottom line: solo and mobile, start on Telegram; team and threads, start on Discord; owner plus staff, run both. That is the whole call on Hermes Agent Discord vs Telegram.

Is Discord or Telegram better for Hermes Agent?

Telegram is better for one person who wants a quick phone line to the agent. Discord is better for teams that need threads, roles and voice channels. Both carry the full Hermes toolset.

Can Hermes Agent use Telegram and Discord at the same time?

Yes. One hermes gateway process runs both adapters, and skills, memory and cron jobs are shared between them.

Why does my Telegram bot ignore messages in a group?

Privacy mode is on by default. Turn it off in BotFather under Group Privacy and re-add the bot, or make the bot a group admin.

Why is my Hermes Discord bot offline?

Message Content Intent is almost always off. Turn it on under Privileged Gateway Intents in the Discord Developer Portal and save.

Discord, by default: 32 MiB per attachment. Telegram’s public Bot API stops at 20 MB unless you run a local telegram-bot-api server, which allows 2 GB.

main once more.
